news_drafts.headline: Caerphilly Council faces £2.9m overspend as schools reserves plunge into deep deficit
news_drafts.lead: Caerphilly Council is projecting a £2.867m overspend for 2026/27, with core funding from council tax and government grants falling short even after the council commits £1.050m from its reserves. Adult services and children's services are driving the largest spending pressures, overspending by £1.206m combined. Meanwhile, the council's schools reserves—money set aside for education—are forecast to fall into a deficit of £14.127m by March 2028, a ringfenced account that cannot be covered from the council's main budget. Capital reserves are being depleted systematically, declining from £27.123m to zero by 2030. The council also faces pressure from a 44% increase in building cleaning costs and has removed two specialist education support services entirely: the Central Behaviour Support Service and Specialist Support Team.

news_drafts.headline: Caerphilly faces £2.867m budget overspend and schools crisis reaching £14.127m deficit by 2028
news_drafts.lead: Caerphilly Council expects to spend £506.476m against a revised budget of £503.609m in 2026/27, leaving a shortfall of £2.867m. Adult Services is overspending by £0.709m and Children's Services by £0.497m, driven by demand-led pressures. The council planned to fill this gap through savings, but its £12.33m savings programme is running 22 percent off-track, with £2.67m of the savings either undelivered or at risk. Schools reserves (money the council has set aside for schools' day-to-day costs) are already in deficit by £0.374m and are forecast to reach a deficit of £14.127m by March 2028, remaining at that level through 2030. Because these reserves are separate from the council's main budget, they cannot be covered by other council spending, leaving a funding gap that the council does not expect to recover.

findings.headline: Council proposing voluntary termination of School PFI contract with material financial implications to follow
findings.detail: External advisor costs for PFI termination have already been incurred and are reflected in the outturn. A further report will set out termination costs, value for money analysis, and potential revenue savings. The full financial impact is not yet quantified.
findings.matters: Major financial and operational decision with termination costs ahead and ongoing revenue implications. Termination of PFI could free up future revenue or create one-off costs depending on terms.
findings.figures: No termination cost yet disclosed; advisor costs included in outturn
findings.quote: An overspend relating to the proposed voluntary termination of the Council's School PFI contract. The current pressure reflects external advisor costs incurred to date. A further report will be presented to Council in due course setting out the full financial implications, including termination costs, value for money considerations and potential revenue savings.

findings.headline: HRA sinking fund for SE Wales PFI fully depleted, creating identified medium-term cashflow pressure
findings.detail: The sinking fund for the South East Wales PFI was fully exhausted in 2025/26. Council has modelled this as a medium-term cashflow pressure and incorporated it into future MTFP budgets, though it is expected to return to surplus in the longer term.
findings.matters: Confirms PFI affordability strain. Cashflow pressure will require either service choices or additional funding for the next several years.
findings.quote: the South East Wales (SEW) PFI sinking fund has been fully depleted, resulting in an in -year overspend. Current financial modelling indicates a medium-term cashflow pressure, which has been incorporated within future years' budgets

findings.headline: £2.059m of £21.280m savings target unachieved, with £0.257m unresolved for 2027/28
findings.detail: 90.3% of savings delivered. Of the £2.059m shortfall, £0.913m is delayed to 2026/27 and £0.889m was addressed through budget pressures in the approved MTFP. However, £0.257m of unachieved savings remains to be resolved in the 2027/28 budget-setting process.
findings.matters: Indicates savings plans are not tracking as anticipated. Unresolved items will create future budget pressure or require new savings elsewhere.
findings.figures: £21.280m total target; £19.221m achieved (90.3%); £2.059m unachieved; £0.913m delayed; £0.889m addressed via budget pressures; £0.257m unresolved
findings.quote: £2.059m of savings were not achieved... £0.913m is expected to be delivered in 2026/27... A total of £0. 889m has been addressed through 2026/27 budget pressures... The remaining £0.257m will need to be considered as part of the 2027/28 budget setting process.

findings.headline: HRA working balances depleted from £26.682m to £3.894m through capital drawdown
findings.detail: The housing revenue account drew £24m for capital and £5.368m additional drawdown in 2025/26. Even after the £1.196m in-year underspend, reserves stand at only £3.894m. This leaves minimal headroom for future capital needs without additional borrowing.
findings.matters: Significant reduction in HRA financial flexibility. Future capital investment or service pressures will require borrowing or service reductions.
findings.figures: Opening balances £26.682m, closing £3.894m; £24m drawn for capital, £5.368m drawdown
findings.quote: HRA Working balances at the start of 2025/26 financial year were £26.682m... When adding the in-year surplus of £1.196m, and re-profiling £0.016m reserves, balances now stand at £3.894m.

findings.headline: Schools collective balances swung from £1.9m surplus to £0.375m deficit in one year
findings.detail: 30 of 82 schools reported deficits totalling £7.773m; the remaining 52 schools had surpluses of £7.398m. The £2.345m overspend in schools was drawn from school balances. The council notes this deteriorating position is expected to continue into 2026/27.
findings.matters: Schools funding has moved into structural deficit requiring subsidy. This signals deteriorating education funding across the council and ongoing demand pressures.
findings.figures: £1.9m surplus (2024/25) to £0.375m deficit (2025/26); 30 schools in deficit; £7.773m collective deficits; £2.345m schools overspend
findings.quote: the collective school bala nces position has moved from a £1.9m surplus at the end of 2024/25 to a deficit of £0.375m at the end of 2025/26
